newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's monetary policy tight - Finance's Werner.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's monetary policy tight - Finance's Werner.

text.p: Mexico's monetary policy remains on the tight side, rather than being in a loose stance, Mexico's deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said in a conference call with financial analysts on Wednesday.
Media reports on Wednesday said monetary policy run by Banco de Mexico was on the lax side in an attempt to boost the economy before July 6 elections.
"It is not a view that we share here," Werner said. "The policy they are running is tight."
"We do not share the view that the policy is lax, in fact, it is the opposite," Werner said.
At the start of the year, the central bank published a list of projected levels for the monetary base. The actual levels have been above the projected levels for much of May.
Central bank officials have said the increase is due to increased demand for cash, which they have met by increasing the monetary base.
Werner also said they see inflation coming down sharply in Mexico.
"We feel the numbers for May will be good, and better than April," Werner said.
In April, the consumer price index rose 1.08 percent.
